non_goals: The ask footer itself — #628 already owns it (assembleAskBody takes postalAddress and fails closed on null/blank)
Dispatch-time byte-match re-assertion of the address against the approved bytes (spec 622 par.7.6 point 3) — #630
Anything in spec 622 par.1/2/5/7.1/7.3/9 — the MessagingAdapter seam, sending domain, env vars and webhook lane are #657
Blocking watch-mode batch construction — the batch still builds; only the send handoff is withheld
Adding a WITHHOLD_REASONS member — the enum is closed, precedence-ordered and versioned by RESTRAINT_POLICY_VERSION, and every member is a per-candidate reason while this is a per-location fact
Any new env var, feature flag or analytics event — the durable attestation record is the columns themselves
Structured international address validation (spec 622 par.7.5 calls it a trap; US-first)
Surfacing the withheld-handoff reason in owner UI on the Requests surface — #629 owns that copy

Re-litigating any decision locked during grilling — the settings/profile surface, withhold-the-handoff-not-the-build, migration 099 behind #645, no-FK attested-by. Recorded on ticket #656 and map #617
user_visible_behavior: An owner sees a solicitation postal address field on settings/profile for their COOKIE-RESOLVED active location, prefilled from google_place_address as an editable suggestion
The owner cannot save the address without ticking an explicit attestation checkbox whose label is POSTAL_ADDRESS_ATTESTATION_TEXT verbatim
Editing a saved address requires a FRESH attestation action; the previously checked state never authorizes edited bytes
An address that is blank, has fewer than two non-empty lines, or has no postal code is rejected with a reason before it is stored
A location with no attested postal address, or with owner_email_bounced TRUE, produces its watch-mode batch and Spoilage report as before but enqueues no ask-generation work
invariants: Tenant isolation: every read and write is scoped by account_id AND the cookie-resolved currentLocationId from requireOwnerAccess — never the account primary location, which would write the wrong location in multi-location accounts

A stored postal address always carries an attestation that covers ITS CURRENT BYTES — not merely a complete tuple. Enforced in the schema by an attested-bytes digest column CHECKed against sha256 of the stored address, so an address-only UPDATE by ANY writer fails closed. Tuple-completeness alone is insufficient: attestPostalAddress behaving well constrains no other writer

attested_by_user_id is a plain UUID point-in-time capture with NO FK — migration 093's documented lesson after 086's ON DELETE CASCADE meant deleting a staff member deleted their uploads. Because there is no FK, the writer must itself verify the actor exists and belongs to the account
Watch-mode is not regressed: buildSolicitationBatch is one builder shared by both modes, so the precondition attaches to the send-only seam and never to closedGateReason
A withheld send handoff writes NO generate_solicitation_asks outbox row, and leaves every per-candidate ask decision and every withheldByReason count byte-identical to the un-withheld cohort
Domain modules receive their DB client as an explicit parameter; only composition roots import the singleton (invariant #15)
Server-authoritative: no NEXT_PUBLIC_* companion (invariant #13). The attester is the authenticated users.id, never a body-supplied value
Vercel is UI only — no LLM, external API or long-running work added to any Next.js route (invariant #1)
edge_cases: google_place_address is a service-area value like 'Austin, TX, USA' — prefill still offered, lint rejects it on save, never silently stored
A five-digit street number must not be mistaken for a postal code; two lines means two NON-EMPTY lines

The offboarding purge NULLs google_place_address today; all attestation columns must be cleared in the SAME statement or the CHECK rejects the row, for EVERY location in the account, and never across tenants
The attesting user is later deleted — the complete attestation tuple survives unchanged, because there is no FK
A re-attestation that fails part-way must leave the previous tuple byte-for-byte intact
A re-attestation by a different user records the NEW actor, not the original one
A client submits an unknown or stale attestation version — refused, so a client can never assent to one text while the server records another
owner_email_bounced and a missing address both apply — first-match precedence reports postal_address_missing only
SOLICITATION_SEND_ENABLED is off (prod today): sendHandoff is exactly not_applicable, the batch still builds, and no generation row exists
The send-handoff enqueue fails — the whole batch build transaction rolls back; a built batch with no generation work is not a reachable state
ask-generation's to_jsonb shim exists solely because the column did not exist; it must be deleted, not left as a fallback

rollback_plan: Revert the PR. Migration 099 is purely additive — five nullable columns on businesses plus two CHECKs constraining only those columns against each other and against the stored address — so it is inert with the code reverted and needs no down migration; dropping the columns would be a separate deliberate migration. SOLICITATION_SEND_ENABLED is off in every environment, so the send-handoff suppression is unreachable in prod either way. Order: apply 099 to staging Supabase first, ride staging, then prod Supabase in lockstep at promotion. MERGE ORDER: #645 (migration 098) merges BEFORE this branch — verify 098 and its migrations-log entry exist before recording head 099.
observability: A send_handoff field on the existing 'solicitation batch build finished' structured log emitted by worker/jobs/solicitation-batch/index.ts, carrying the location-level withheld reason alongside business_id and no contact PII — the signal that a location is silently not sending. Emitted by the worker, NOT by batch-builder.ts, which returns results and deliberately does no logging
The attestation columns themselves are the durable record: querying businesses for solicitation_postal_address_attested_at answers 'which locations may send' directly, with no derived state to drift
A 4xx rate on PUT /api/settings/postal-address indicates the lint is rejecting real owner addresses — the signal that the US-first lint is too strict for the live customer mix
